holes: liveness: a child is seen only if it is alive at a snapshot (or has a Sysmon 1 event), and a connection only while it is open; one that ended between snapshots is not seen. An agent between two requests owns no connection, so its acts go to a talking ancestor: what is left of its talk (a TIME-WAIT row with no owner, a DNS cache row with no pid) is shown as recent talk, owner unknown, never as a candidate, and its tree can be an act-root (talk not seen)
sibling talkers: the talker must be an ancestor of the child; a talker beside it (an Electron network process, a local daemon or proxy that relays the model) is not joined to it
reparented acts: a child started with setsid, nohup or a double fork, or whose parent exited (reparented to init; on Windows a dead parent's pid can be reused), is not attributed
TCP only: UDP and QUIC (HTTP/3) and unix-socket relays to a local proxy are not read as talk
one view: sockets of other network namespaces (containers) and processes hidden by hidepid or by another user's /proc permissions are not seen
Linux: no offline name record in M5.0, so endpoints match by IP network and loopback port only (ADR-0004)
Linux: argv[0] and status Name are written by the process itself, and a copied shell takes any name; the /proc/PID/exe link places a process for act-root (G-2), the names still come from argv[0]
no file-write record (Sysmon 11): a talker that acts only by writing files, with no child, is not seen
